title: Prompt and output security
summary: Separate instruction manipulation from downstream security impact.
html:
Objectives

  • Distinguish direct and indirect inputs.
  • Separate model behavior from unauthorized application actions.
  • Check how generated text becomes HTML, queries, or commands.

Concepts and boundaries

Direct prompt injection arrives through the user interface; indirect injection arrives through material the system reads, such as a document or tool result. Jailbreaking concerns attempts to circumvent a model’s behavioral constraints. These can overlap, but a security assessment should identify the actual application impact rather than counting every changed answer as a compromise.

Output handling is a separate boundary. Even a well-behaved model can produce malformed data. Rendering generated HTML, constructing a query, or executing a proposed command without validation can turn an answer into an application vulnerability. A disclosed system instruction may reveal useful implementation detail, but its exposure alone does not prove access to protected data.

Practice checklist

Use an isolated lab or an explicitly authorized environment. Record prerequisites and configuration before changing inputs.

  1. Create a disposable local document containing only a harmless marker such as TEST-MARKER-42.
  2. Establish a baseline answer for a task that summarizes that document. Record the original request and output.
  3. Add a benign instruction asking the assistant to include the marker, then repeat the same task. Compare direct input with retrieved-document input.
  4. Trace where the answer goes. In a local test renderer, verify that text resembling markup is displayed as text rather than interpreted as active content.
  5. Record the exact instruction placement, output, application behavior, and repeated-trial count.

Expected observations

The marker demonstrates influence, not data theft or code execution. Identify whether the application merely echoed text or crossed a protected boundary. A renderer that safely escapes output should not turn generated markup into an executable action.

Mitigations and retesting

Enforce permissions outside the model, keep secrets out of prompts, validate structured outputs, and apply context-appropriate escaping. Instruction reminders and keyword filters alone are not a complete authorization mechanism.
